archetype.name: Playoff Team (defense-first, shorthanded)
archetype.definition: A recent champion whose rim protection still travels but whose offense has fallen to the bottom third of the league while two core pieces have played only half its games, leaving a 4-2 record that flatters a break-even margin.

report.headline: A champion's defense, a lottery offense, and a 4-2 record that flatters both
report.take:
Oklahoma City arrives at 4-2 with a recent pedigree behind it: 68-14 and a title two seasons ago, 64-18 and the league's top defense last year. Six games in, the site has it 21st of 30, and the margin explains why. The Thunder have been outscored by 3 points overall, their Net Rtg is -0.5 (17th), and the point differential implies three wins, not four. The early record rests on a 4-0 start that included a 12-point win over Denver. The last two games, at Dallas (96-120) and at Houston (98-119), were blowouts.

The split between the two ends is stark. The defense is still a real asset. Its 109.6 defensive rating ranks 9th, opponents shoot 58.2% at the rim (2nd in the league, about seven points under the league average), and opponents' eFG % of 51 ranks 6th. The offense is the problem. Its 109.1 rating ranks 23rd, after 118.9 last season. The Thunder rank 28th in eFG %, 26th in 3P %, 29th in 3PA Rate and 28th in FT Rate. They are not taking threes, not making the ones they take, and not getting to the line, so nearly every possession rests on Shai Gilgeous-Alexander creating something in the midrange. His 32.8 USG % and +21.7 On-Off show how much the team leans on him. His 55.2 TS % shows that even he has not been able to carry it efficiently.

The context the raw numbers hide is availability. Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren have each played only three of the six games. Holmgren's +6.4 On-Off is the best of the frontcourt, and his absence is a large part of why that group grades a D. Their minutes have gone to Jared McCain (47.5 TS %, -5.7 BPM) and Jaylin Williams (33.6 TS %), and those two have been the biggest drags on an offense that cannot afford them. Ajay Mitchell has been the bright spot: 5th of 110 on the shooting-guard tab with a 4.6 BPM, a legitimate second creator.

The read: this is not a 55-win team on current form, as the margin says, but the six-game offense is not who it is either. The shooting rates are well below anything in its recent history, and the defensive identity has held up. The question is how fast a healthy Holmgren and Jalen Williams pull the offense back toward the middle of the league. A week with Cleveland twice and an unbeaten Memphis will test that before the answer arrives.

strengths.title: Rim protection still elite
strengths.body: Opponents shoot 58.2% at the rim, 2nd in the league. They also get there less often than average, with an Opp Rim Rate ranked 7th. This is the backbone of a top-10 defense even with Holmgren in and out, and it fits a franchise that ranked 1st in defense in each of the last two seasons. It should hold, and it should get stronger as Holmgren plays more.

strengths.title: Gilgeous-Alexander and Mitchell carry the creation
strengths.body: The offense collapses without its star: the team is 21.7 points per 100 possessions better with Gilgeous-Alexander on the floor. Mitchell, 5th on the shooting-guard tab with a 4.6 BPM and 58.2 TS %, gives it a second ball-handler who has actually been efficient. Their partnership is the most reliable thing the team has right now.

strengths.title: Possessions protected and extended
strengths.body: A TOV % of 12.9 (7th) and an ORB % of 28.5 (10th) mean the Thunder rarely waste trips and often get second chances. That is how an offense this poor at shooting has stayed afloat. Low turnovers have been a constant in its recent history, so this edge is real.

concerns.title: Shot profile has gone flat
concerns.body: The Thunder rank 29th in 3PA Rate, 26th in 3P % and 28th in FT Rate, adding up to a 28th-ranked eFG %. Too much of the offense is being funneled through tough twos. Some of the 3P % will bounce back with sample size. The low volume from three and at the line is structural until the lineup gets healthier.

concerns.title: Record outrunning the margin
concerns.body: A minus-3 point differential supports three wins, and the W vs Pt Diff of 1 ranks 2nd in the league. The two most recent games were lopsided road losses, and the last five games come out to -3 a game. Until the margin turns positive, the 4-2 is a soft number.

concerns.title: Thin frontcourt without Holmgren
concerns.body: The frontcourt grades a D. Jaylin Williams (33.6 TS %, -5.3 BPM) and Aday Mara (-4.2 BPM) have absorbed heavy minutes. Holmgren has played only three games, and his +6.4 On-Off leads the group. This lasts exactly as long as his absences do.

trend.note: A 4-0 start built mostly at home gave way to back-to-back road losses by 24 and 21. The last five games run three points a game worse than the season as a whole.

weekAhead.headline: Cleveland twice, then the unbeaten league leader on the road
weekAhead.body:
Three of the four games are against top-10 teams on the site. Cleveland (7th, 4-2, Net Rtg 4.9) comes first in a home-and-home. Memphis is 6-0, first on the site, and ranks 1st in Net Rtg at 15.1, with top-two ratings on both ends. Washington closes the week at home and is the softest game on paper. Even so, the Wizards' defense allows the lowest opponent eFG % in the league, which is a bad matchup for a team shooting this poorly.

The pattern to watch is guard pressure. Cleveland holds point guards well under their usual scoring, and Washington allows the second-fewest points to the position. That makes Gilgeous-Alexander's week harder and puts more on Mitchell and on whoever is healthy in the frontcourt. A split of the four would be a reasonable outcome. Two wins against Cleveland would be a real signal.

keyMatchups.title: Hartenstein against a soft middle
keyMatchups.body: Cleveland's A+ frontcourt is strong in its own right, but its defense gives up 22.67 points a game to centers, 27th in the league. That is far above what those centers score elsewhere. With guards likely to be crowded, the Thunder bigs, Hartenstein (58.4 TS %) in particular, have a real opening in both games.

keyMatchups.title: Memphis shooting vs. average perimeter defense
keyMatchups.body: Memphis leads the league at 41.7% from three. The Thunder's Opp 3P % of 35.3 sits mid-pack at 17th, a contrast with their elite rim defense. If the Grizzlies get their looks from deep, the paint protection matters less, and a low-volume Thunder offense cannot win a shootout.

keyMatchups.title: Second chances against Washington
keyMatchups.body: Washington ranks 28th in DRB % and 29th in ORB %. The Thunder's 10th-ranked offensive rebounding is how they beat a defense that otherwise suffocates shooters. Winning the glass is the cleanest path to a win at home.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Holmgren and Jalen Williams are both in the lineup, and whether the 3PA Rate climbs when they are.

restOfSeason.body:
The defense is the sustainable part: rim protection at this level has been the franchise's signature for two years, and it should keep the floor high. The offense will improve, because shooting this far below the team's recent norms rarely holds, and more Holmgren and Jalen Williams minutes push McCain and Jaylin Williams down the rotation. The close-game edge, by contrast, should fade. I expect a team that wins on the margin rather than by luck, somewhere around 50 to 58 wins, with a Net Rtg settling at +3 to +8 and an offensive rating climbing back into the 113-117 range.

The ceiling depends on health more than anything in these six games. A full-strength version looks like the 60-win teams in its history. A version that keeps leaning on Gilgeous-Alexander's usage behind a D frontcourt is a mid-pack playoff team.

confidence.note: Six games, two key players in only half of them.
